messages.subject: Degree day calculation
parts:
Hi All,

I'm new to Davis R group (and also to R) and will be participation in the meeting next quarter. Meanwhile, I have the following question and appreciate any help:

I'm working on my data and getting stock in making a function that could calculate the degree days between planting and heading (Heading1 file attached). I have calculated the daily degree day (bavg column in temp3 file) but I can't get the function work to extract the cumulative degree day between my planting and heading dates or in other word, I would like to make function that can calculate and return cumulative degree day for 45 planting to heading dates base on daily temperature. Attached file has the temperature data (Temp3), planting to heading dates (Heading1), and my codes so far (codes_heading).

Thanks,
Hussain

messages.subject: Re: Degree day calculation
parts:
Hi Hussain,
Didn't have a lot of time to look at this...but my solution is below. It's not elegant but I believe it works. You shouldn't use cumsum() across the whole temperature (bavg) column as it will cumulatively sum the entire column, without regard to different plots and restarts.

A solution is using ave(): 
e$t <- ave(e$bavg, e$ID, FUN = cumsum)

This breaks out each group (plot?) and then calculates the cumulative sum over that group.

Instead of a function I just merged the datasets together and pulled the data needed, hopefully ID is unique and I understood your question correctly.

tst<-merge(e,h,by="ID",all=T) # merge the datasets by ID
dim(tst) # make sure the dimensions look correct
start<-tst[tst$date2==tst$jdate,] # pull only rows that match the Planting julian date
end<-tst[tst$date3==tst$jdate,] # pull only rows that match the Heading date
final<-end$t-start$t # calculate the total difference for the cumulative temperatures

I suspect this may need revision! It may make more sense to calculate the degree day temperatures from the initial start date rather than from the beginning of your dataset, which means you can just subset as above and then write a function or re-run the ave() line with some minor changes.

Hope this helps.

Adios,
Ryan
